subject: Materials Science
title: Wind Turbine Blades
description: A short lesson to help you apply Wind Turbine Blades.

hook.text: A wind turbine blade longer than a Boeing 747 wing flexes in every storm and lasts 25 years.

buildup.text: Blades are glass or carbon fiber shells bonded around foam or balsa wood cores.

discovery.text: Composites provide the stiffness-to-weight ratio needed for blades over 100 meters long.

twist.text: End-of-life blades are hard to recycle — glass fiber thermosets resist reprocessing.

climax.text: New thermoplastic blades promise full recyclability — the industry's biggest sustainability challenge.

punchline.text: Composites harvest the wind but leave a recycling puzzle.

quiz.question: Why are composite wind turbine blades hard to recycle?
options: They are too small to process
